proof:
# Binary padding refutes truncated marginal lifting

The proposed auxiliary statement is false:

    max_{x in C_z} depth_mu(z,x)
      >= gamma_d min{1/2, depth_nu(z)}.                (TL)

Here mu is normalized mixed-integer volume and nu is its integer marginal.
The counterexample below has n=2, d=4, positive full-dimensional fibers,
and a chosen integer fiber of marginal depth strictly less than 1/2.
It does not refute OC, because its proposed target is stronger than OC.

## Exact binary-padding lemma

Let rho be any probability measure of compact support in R^m. Give
{0,1} x R^m the probability measure rho'=(delta_0+delta_1)/2 x rho.
For every y in R^m,

    depth_{rho'}(0,y) = depth_rho(y)/2.              (P)

The depths use every closed ambient halfspace. To prove the lower bound,
restrict a halfspace containing (0,y) to its layer with first coordinate
zero. This restriction is a closed halfspace containing y, or all of R^m.
Its rho mass is at least depth_rho(y). The other layer contributes a
nonnegative amount. For the upper bound, take any old containing halfspace
G={w:a dot w>=b}. Compactness of the support allows M>0 such that
a dot w-M<b throughout the support. Then

    G'={(t,w):a dot w-Mt>=b}

agrees with G in layer zero and misses the whole supported layer one.
Thus rho'(G')=rho(G)/2. Take the infimum over G. The proof includes closed
boundaries and does not require an infimum to be attained.

Applying (P) both to mu and to its integer marginal nu proves that if
an untruncated gamma_d*beta lifting assertion fails at a fiber z, then
(TL) fails at the fiber (0,z) after adding one binary integer coordinate:
beta becomes beta/2<=1/2 and every point depth becomes exactly half its
old depth. This is an obstruction to truncation as a repair mechanism.

## A fully specified n=2, d=4 example

Let

    T={x in R^4:x_i>=0, sum_{i=1}^4 x_i<=1},
    lambda_0(x)=1-sum_{i=1}^4 x_i,
    lambda_i(x)=x_i  (1<=i<=4),
    r=1/10, epsilon=r^4=1/10000,
    B={x in T:lambda_0(x)>=1-r}.

Write V=vol_4(T)=1/24. The homothety x->rx maps T onto B, so
vol_4(B)=epsilon V. Define

    D=conv(({-1}xB) union ({0}xT) union ({1}xB)),
    C=[0,1]xD.

The integer coordinates of C are (t,z). Its only nonempty fibers are

    C_(t,-1)=B, C_(t,0)=T, C_(t,1)=B,  t=0,1.

Indeed the endpoint fibers of D must use only the corresponding endpoint
generators, while its middle fiber contains T and is contained in T since
B subset T. C is a compact full-dimensional convex body in R^6, and all
six fibers have positive 4-volume. Its total mixed volume is

    M=2(1+2 epsilon)V.

In the one-dimensional integer marginal of D, the point zero has depth

    beta=(1+epsilon)/(1+2 epsilon)=10001/10002.

This follows immediately from the only two orientations of a real-line
halfspace: either tail containing zero has mass at least the middle fiber
plus one endpoint fiber, and that mass is attained by the tail beginning
at zero. By (P), the marginal of C has depth at (0,0)

    beta'=beta/2=10001/20004<1/2.

Let gamma_4=(4/5)^4=256/625. The proposed normalized target is
gamma_4 beta', whose unnormalized value is

    tau V, where tau=gamma_4(1+epsilon)=160016/390625.

We show that every x in C_(0,0)=T has a closed containing halfspace of
mass strictly less than tau V. For i=0,...,4 use the containing halfspace

    H_i(x)={(t,z,w):lambda_i(w)-2t>=lambda_i(x)}.

Its normal is nonzero, its boundary contains (0,0,x), and it excludes all
of layer t=1, since there lambda_i(w)-2<=-1<0<=lambda_i(x). In layer t=0,
the T-fiber contribution has volume

    (1-lambda_i(x))^4 V.

This cap-volume identity is the homothety of the simplex with center at
vertex i and scale 1-lambda_i(x).

Suppose all five displayed caps had mass at least tau V. On each endpoint
fiber B, lambda_i<=r for i=1,...,4. Therefore, whenever lambda_i(x)>r,
both endpoint contributions vanish and

    lambda_i(x)<=1-tau^(1/4),  i=1,...,4.

The same bound holds if lambda_i(x)<=r, because
tau<(1-r)^4 implies r<1-tau^(1/4). The cap for i=0 captures at most all
the two endpoint fibers, of combined volume 2 epsilon V. It gives

    lambda_0(x)<=1-(tau-2 epsilon)^(1/4).

The following rational certificates imply that these five bounds cannot
sum to one:

    a=8000199/10000000, b=7999223/10000000,
    tau-a^4=2032792963819263760799/10^28>0,
    tau-2 epsilon-b^4=664183074753367294559/10^28>0,
    4a+b-4=19/10000000>0.

Hence

    4 tau^(1/4)+(tau-2 epsilon)^(1/4)>4a+b>4,

whereas summing the five bounds would give

    1=sum_i lambda_i(x)
      <=5-4 tau^(1/4)-(tau-2 epsilon)^(1/4)<1.

This contradiction proves that one of the five explicit closed halfspaces
through every chosen point has normalized mass below gamma_4 beta'. Thus
no point anywhere in the chosen fiber attains (TL). All arithmetic is
checked by ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_truncated_lifting.py using exact rational operations.

For completeness, the maximum is strictly below the proposed target:
each of the five cap masses above is continuous as a function of x in T,
because the relevant four-dimensional hyperplane boundaries have zero
measure. Their minimum is continuous, and T is compact. It is everywhere
strictly below tau V by the contradiction, so its attained maximum is
strictly below tau V. The actual depth is bounded above by this minimum.

Again, gamma_4 beta'>gamma_4/4, the OC target for n=2. This construction
invalidates the proposed strengthening without conflicting with OC.
